headline: Updated asthma guidance changes how children under five are diagnosed
dek: Yixin Tan, editor of Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory, said frequent wheezing, coughing or breathlessness in a child should prompt a medical review, according to The Sector.
body:
Updated asthma guidance changes how children under five are diagnosed, The Sector reported, citing comments by Yixin Tan, editor of Therapeutic Guidelines: Respiratory, to Australian Pharmacist.

Tan said a medical review should take place if a child is frequently experiencing wheezing, coughing or breathlessness. The article noted that parents may notice night-time coughing, while educators may see a child wheezing or pausing to breathe during play. It said both groups can give doctors detailed information on when and how often symptoms occur, and whether they affect the child's sleep or play.

The article said pre-school children often wheeze, particularly when unwell or with a cold, and that one instance of wheezing does not automatically indicate asthma. It added that the standard diagnostic test can be hard to carry out successfully in this age group. GPs can instead observe whether wheezing or breathlessness improves after a reliever inhaler. Where symptoms are common or affect sleep or play, a GP may suggest a trial period of a preventer inhaler.

The article said a pre-school diagnosis does not always mean a child will continue to have asthma, and that parents and GPs can review whether ongoing treatment is still needed.

It also cited Asthma Australia's advice that a child's asthma action plan should be reviewed and amended by a doctor if their asthma or medications change. According to the article, the plan should be available to the child's early learning service so that parents and educators know which medication to give, how to manage a flare-up and when to seek urgent help.
key_quote: one instance of wheezing does not automatically indicate that a child has asthma.

source.title: New updated asthma guidance changes how children under five are diagnosed
